The challenge is to provide an intrinsic geometric inter- pretation of the family of graded linear series *W*• *t*. When *X* = *C₁* ×... ×*Cn*, intersection theory on Bl*xX* implies that*W*• *t* is contained in a family of complete linear series associated to divisors on *X*Σ, the blow-up of P *n*−1 in *n* points in general linear position. We show that this inclusion is asymptotically an equality. For this we use that *X*Σis a toric variety and the asymptotic behaviour of complete linear series on them can be managed through convex geometry. As a consequence, the vertical slices of ∆*x*(*L*) are NObodies associated to a ray of divisors on *X*Σwith respect to a generic (strict transform) linear flag. Lastly, the global (gluing all *t* > 0) NObody on this special ray of divisors on *X*Σis exactly the convex set described in the statement, as we are able to prove the existence of sections whose valuation are the vertices of the simplex. For box-products of arbitrary degrees the vertical slices of ∆*x*(*L*) are still a family of NObodies on *X*Σ with respect to general linear flags. But it is harder to guess the vertices. It seems an interesting problem to find an algorithm that starts with a polytope in R *n*−1 that is a NObody on a toric variety with respect to a *T*-invariant flag, and construct another polytope, that will be a NObody on the same toric space but with respect to a generic linear flag. In dimension *n* 6 3, we can find non-trivial sections on *X*Σ, whose valuations provide the vertices of a slice of the global NObody on *X*Σwith respect to general linear flags. More precisely:

On one hand we have infinitesimal successive minima, then jets and finally polytopal upper and lower bounds on the generic iNObodies. Moreover, in [FL25c] the authors study the shape of generic iNObodies on Jacobians in small dimensions. The main issue here is realizing at least asymptotically the family*W* • *t* as *complete* graded linear series on a modification of P *n*−1. For example, for non-hyperelliptic Jacobian threefolds, *W* • *t* becomes complete on a birational model of P² that is far from being toric, while for the hyperelliptic case we may need to go to the Zariski–Riemann space. The paper is organized as follows. In Section 2 we review the Newton–Okounkov body construction and their basic properties. In Section 3 we use intersection theory, positivity, toric geometry and Euclidean volume computations to understand the vertical slices as Newton–Okounkov bodies on *X*Σ. In Section 4 we treat the case of dimension *n* 6 3. In Section 5 we use particular incomplete linear systems on *X*Σto prove that the vertices of the simplex from Theorem 1.1 do belong to the iNObody, concluding its proof. In Section 6 we state and motivate some open questions.
